claim: The New York Fed Empire State Manufacturing Index surged to 20.6 in August 2026 from 15.6 in July, its highest since late 2021, with new orders at 17.3 and shipments at 11.7, signaling robust demand across the northeastern manufacturing base.
source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

claim: The Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey general activity index jumped to 47.4 in August from 41.4 in July, its highest reading since April 2021, with forward-expectations indexes surging and continued employment gains.

The Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey new orders index jumped sharply to 22 from 5.4 in July and the production index rose to 16.1, signaling a notable acceleration in Texas factory activity for August.
source_name: Fort Worth Inc. / Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas

claim: The Richmond Fed manufacturing shipments index rose to 11 from 8 in July, continuing to signal Fifth District manufacturing expansion heading into the ISM release.
The July 2026 ISM Manufacturing report showed New Orders at 56.7% and Employment at 52.8% (first expansion in 33 months), providing strong momentum across key sub-indices entering August.

The S&P Global Flash US Manufacturing PMI fell to 53.2 in August from 53.9 in July, a five-month low, with factory output at its weakest since July 2025 and new order growth at its slowest since March, indicating broad manufacturing momentum cooled.

The S&P Global Flash PMI report confirmed that new order growth was at its slowest since March and inventories contracted for the first time since February, suggesting pipeline demand may be softening ahead of the ISM release.
The July 2026 ISM Prices Index remained highly elevated at 71.1%, signaling persistent input cost pressures that could dampen production decisions and compress margins for manufacturers in August.

The July 2026 ISM Supplier Deliveries Index at 58.9% was elevated, reflecting supply-chain tightening that can represent a transitory boost to the composite and may normalize downward in August, reducing the headline.
